title: Research: seven-source singleton universal path — length 18 excluded, f(7) >= 20 (no new kappa)
body:
# Seven-source singleton universal path: `f(7) >= 20` (no new kappa)

Contributor: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance in scoping, implementation, verification and writing; no independent human review claimed). No kappa, supplier, certificate or selected-frontier change.

## Change and mathematical scope

In the PR943 prefix-walk model ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943), `research/universal-connector-boundary`), a restored source word `w` over `n` singleton labels is universal when paired readouts realize every mask, `D(w) = {q_s xor q_t} = F2^n`; `f(n)` is the minimum universal word length. The pinned record ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1185](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1185), `research/universal-connector-six-source`) leaves `18 <= f(7) <= 24` with `f(7)` explicitly open. This package removes 18:

> **No universal seven-source word of length 18 exists. Hence `f(7) >= 20` and the gap is `20 <= f(7) <= 24`.**

The alphabet is singletons only. The charged DUO pair-source family ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2396](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2396), [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2128](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2128), [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2156](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2156)) and the 63-mask weight-1/2/3 sparse family ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2229](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2229), [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2236](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2236), [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2397](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2397)) are distinct scopes and are recorded as concurrent, not overlapping.

## Method

Smallest falsifying instance first: the engine rebuilds the pinned `research/universal-connector-six-source/EXPECTED.json` byte-for-byte (945 words max 31/32; 10,395 words max 49/64; 945,945 words max 59/64; records SHA-256 `3dcc5689…`, `491b295f…`, `3d711ffa…`), plus the counting lower bounds 10/14/18 and the Gray constructions. The pinned record is `f(5) = 12`, `f(6) = 16`; the assignment's placeholder values were corrected by reading the pinned packages.

Then the length-18 census at `n = 7`, via the prefix vertex set `P = E union O` (even/odd weight):

1. Position parity gives `|E|, |O| <= 9`; counting gives `|E||O| >= 64`, `C(|E|,2) + C(|O|,2) >= 63`.
2. A pair-representation identity (machine-checked rows in `CERTIFICATE.json`, independently re-derived by collision-multiset enumeration) contradicts the 17-point splits `(9,8)` and `(8,9)`: full odd coverage forces `sum_x A_x B_x >= 4`, full even coverage bounds the same sum by 1. So `|P| = 18` and every universal 18-word would walk a simple 18-cycle with the forced `(9,9)` split and collision budget `e_ex + b_ex <= 9`.
3. `engine.cyclic_census(7, 18, budget=9, simple=True)` exhausts the restricted-growth direction words (complete under coordinate relabeling, a hypercube automorphism) with those proved-necessary prunes: **15,775,992 nodes, 312,064 simple 18-cycles, 0 universal words.** Shards partition the tree; leaf counts agree with an unsharded run exactly.

Controls and non-vacuity: the cyclic census's leaf set equals the reference canonical word set exactly at `n = 5` length 10 and `n = 6` length 12; zero universal words at `n = 5` length 10 and `n = 6` length 14 reproduces `f(5) = 12`, `f(6) = 16` from the other side; planted hits are found at `n = 5` length 12 and `n = 6` length 16 and re-checked; the set-level engine agrees with a brute-force census of all 20,160,075 ten-point sets of `F2^5` (99,200 covers, none cycle-realisable) and reproduces the community nine-point result (7,888,725 sets, max 29, zero covers, [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18931315](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18931315)). `independent.py` re-checks coverage with the dual predicate, realizes cycles with subset dynamic programming, and re-derives the identity rows without the closed-form bound.

## Reproduction and checks

From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/universal-f7-singleton-seedb859517b/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/universal-f7-singleton-seedb859517b/independent.py
python3 -I -B research/universal-f7-singleton-seedb859517b/test_engine.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/universal-f7-singleton-seedb859517b --check-only
```

Observed markers:

```text
PASS_F7_SINGLETON_GAP_VERIFY f(7) >= 20 (length 18 excluded) cycles=312064 universal_words=0 nodes=15775992 seconds=72.2
PASS_F7_INDEPENDENT {"control_sets": "ok", "lemma_rows": {...}, "witnesses_replayed": 0}
Ran 22 tests in 154.694s — OK
PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
```

The decisive census is `search.py` (about 15 minutes, resumable from per-shard checkpoints): `PASS_F7_SINGLETON_GAP f(7)>=20 L18-excluded`.

## Scope and open questions

A finite exclusion inside PR943's abstract interface; no instantiation in the selected supplier and no kappa claim. Open: whether a universal seven-source singleton word of length 20 or 22 exists or the Gray bound 24 is sharp; and whether any 18-point cover of `F2^7` exists at all (the set-level restricted addition basis value `r((C2)^7)`, whose six-source analogue the community records as 14 after Gavrylkiv). Structured next questions are in `TASK.json` and the package README.
